name: Cerro La Campana by the Andinista trail
why: Darwin climbed it in 1834: from the summit you see the Pacific and Aconcagua in the same look.
book: CONAF entry at the Granizo sector, Olmué (tickets on Pases Parques). The top part, from the mine to the summit, closes June to August.
water: None after the start: carry 3 litres, it is hot.
dangers: The top part is a rock scramble with your hands.
Summer heat and no shade low down: go in spring or autumn.
Snow, wind and lightning on the summit in winter.

points.name: Sector Granizo, La Campana National Park
points.note: The CONAF entrance and ranger post at Granizo, Olmué, about 400 m; the Andinista trail leaves the road above the campsites.

points.name: Darwin plaque, Cerro La Campana
points.note: About 1,530 m, past the old La Pronosticada mine: the plaque for Darwin's climb of 17 August 1834.

points.name: Cerro La Campana summit
points.note: 1,880 m: the Pacific to the west, Aconcagua to the east.
